display.purpose: Storefront hero headline only - one use per page, at most.

headline.purpose: Page-level titles on content pages (contact, newsletter, legal, error/placeholder states).

title.purpose: Admin page titles and in-page section headers.

body.purpose: Primary and secondary copy; PDP descriptions.

label.purpose: Brand kickers, section labels, stock/status text, table headers - always via the Eyebrow primitive.

mono.purpose: Reserved for tabular numerals (price, quantity, counts), never run as body text.

motion.name: feedback
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus feedback for color, background, and opacity changes.

motion.name: large-surface
motion.purpose: Large-surface moments, e.g. the product-card image hover-zoom.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.value: transform: scale(0.97) button / scale(0.94) icon button
motion.purpose: Active/press feedback in place of a color change.

motion.name: morph
motion.value: 320ms View Transition with a mid-flight blur keyframe
motion.purpose: Signature catalog/related card -> PDP gallery image hand-off.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation, including the signature morph, collapses under reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Prominent CTA register - hero, "Add to bag".
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; border: none; border-radius: 0; transition: opacity 0.15s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Bordered, transparent-fill counterpart to the primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: border-color 0.15s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Active-filter / state-as-label chip - no color coding, weight and fill only.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); border-radius: 0; transition: background-color 0.15s; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The one containment device in the system: a flat, bordered panel.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0; padding: 24px; }

components.name: Input
components.description: Text field - flat, bordered, focus signaled by border color plus the global outline.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 14px; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Eyebrow Label
components.description: Wide-tracked uppercase micro-label used for brand kickers, section labels, and status text.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--muted-foreground); }

components.name: The Doxa Face
components.description: The system's one illustrated signature - a stroke-only watch case drawn as a face, shown here in its calm (10:10) mood. Used across empty and error states.

narrative.overview: Doxa reads like tools laid out in precise, deliberate order on a bench: nothing decorative, nothing that isn't load-bearing. Every surface is flat, every edge is a straight 1px line, and the only accent is ink-on-paper (or paper-on-ink in dark mode) - there is no hue doing semantic work anywhere in the system, not even for errors. Hierarchy comes from weight, tracking, and restraint rather than color or shadow. Wide-tracked uppercase micro-labels stand in for the legends and gauge-markings a bench of precision instruments would carry. This is a real, pre-launch commerce product built on trust through price/value transparency, not a portfolio piece - the visual language is doing real work: a shopper who isn't a watch expert should feel like nothing is being hidden or oversold to them. The system rejects both directions a watch retailer could default to: the gold-gradient, serif-heavy "heritage luxury" cliche, and the bright, rounded, playful DTC-ecommerce default. It sits deliberately between them - serious but not ornate, warm but not cute. Motion is not an afterthought bolted onto a static system; it is one of the system's few expressive tools precisely because color isn't available for that job. Use it deliberately and consistently, never decoratively.
keyCharacteristics: Zero border-radius on every structural surface; radius is reserved for two narrow exceptions (icon affordances, circular swatches/avatars).
Containment is always a 1px border - there are no shadows anywhere in the system.
No semantic color: state is signaled through weight, underline, opacity, and fill only.
Wide-tracked uppercase micro-labels (Eyebrow) do the work color-coding would do elsewhere.
One illustrated signature (The Doxa Face) stands in for every icon/illustration need tied to system or empty states - no emoji, no stock icon sets.
Motion is purposeful and consistent: short, functional transitions plus one signature view-transition morph, never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Ink Discipline Rule
rules.body: Ink (the accent) never appears as a large fill. It marks a single active/selected/primary element at a time - a filled button, a selected swatch, a solid badge, a focus outline. If a screen needs to signal more than one thing at once, reach for weight or a border, not a second use of Ink.

rules.name: The No Hue Rule
rules.body: There is no red/green/amber anywhere in the system, including for form errors and destructive actions. Errors are text-foreground underline decoration-2 underline-offset-2; disabled is opacity-40; selected is border-accent (plus bg-accent text-accent-foreground when it must read fully "on"). A genuinely new severity need is a design decision to raise explicitly, not a reach for red-500.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every text role is Mona Sans. A second typeface is never introduced to signal hierarchy - size, weight, tracking, and case already do that job.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Price, quantity, and count digits always carry tabular-nums so they don't visually jitter as they update or align in a column.

rules.name: The Border-Only Rule
rules.body: If something needs to look contained, separated, or "above" its surroundings, the answer is a 1px border, never a shadow. This is an invariant, not a starting point to relax later.

rules.name: The Purposeful Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion always marks a real state change or hand-off (hover, press, selection, a navigation transition) - never runs as ambient decoration. Consistency and restraint matter more than novelty: reuse the existing duration/easing vocabulary before inventing a new one.

dos: Do use a 1px border-border for every containment need - cards, inputs, dividers, panels.
Do route all text through the five typographic roles (Display/Headline/Title/Body/Label) and their exact weight/tracking values rather than picking an arbitrary size.
Do signal state (error, disabled, selected, active) through weight, underline, opacity, or fill - never through hue.
Do keep motion purposeful and consistent with the existing duration/easing vocabulary (150ms feedback, 500ms large-surface, the 320ms morph).
Do reach for The Doxa Face before any other icon/illustration for empty or error states.
donts: Don't add shadow-* utilities anywhere - depth is a border, never a shadow.
Don't add a radius to a structural surface (buttons, inputs, cards, chips, panels) - the only exceptions are small icon affordances and circular elements.

Don't reach for red-500/green-500/amber-500 or any semantic hue for errors, warnings, or success states - use weight/underline/opacity/fill instead, and raise a genuinely new severity need as a design decision first.
Don't drift toward gold-gradient "heritage luxury" styling or bright, rounded, playful DTC-ecommerce styling - the system sits deliberately between both.
Don't introduce a second illustration style, emoji, or stock icon set alongside The Doxa Face.
Don't animate decoratively - every transition should be traceable to a real state change or hand-off.
